newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates ease, interest for tonnage wane.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates ease, interest for tonnage wane.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were steady to weaker on Wednesday with enough tonnage seen available to meet subdued enquiries with the exception of tonnage from the Middle East Gulf to Japan and Eastern Asia which saw firmer fixtures, shipping brokers said.
Two VLCCs were fixed into Japan from the Middle East Gulf at W67, up two points from Tuesday's levels. Fixtures into Singapore were also some 2.5 points firmer at W62.5.
"Mideast-Asia is the exception and in other places the rates are falling. You have cross Med at just under W100 and cross U.K. at W105," a shipping broker said.
He said Mobil was enquiring into a VLCC for Singapore for Nov 25/26 and the market would be looking at the number for direction.
Brokers attributed weaker sentiment elsewhere to available tonnage for the rest of November and early December with fewer enquiries as traders wrapped up business for the year.
Another said it was a combination of a build up of tonnage and slack trade.
Cross-Med business was weaker with Suezmaxes seen at no higher than W95 after business on Tuesday at W97.5. A broker said Aframax tonnage was valued 2.5 points either side of W105.

"Russian enquiry is not as active as it has been. Modern ships are quite readily available and there is less pressure on charterers," another shipping broker said. "What has been done recently in the Med was for longer journeys and charterers are happier to waive a premium on these voyages."

North Sea, Inter UKC trade for 80,000 tonne business was also weaker at around W105 after Tuesday's fixture at W112.5. Transatlantic rates were steady at W65 and W90 for VLCCs and Suezmax respectively but few enquiries were heard.
West African trade was thin. Glencore fixed a VLCC for Dec 1 to India at $975,000. -- Kate Dourian, London +44 171 542 4088
